positions.source_passage: To ensure continuous safety, effectiveness, and auditability, manufacturers must employ combination strategies involving localized model locking, strict QMS version lifecycle management, and continuous automated drift detection.
positions.position_gist: Manufacturers should use a combination of localized model locking, QMS version lifecycle management, and continuous automated drift detection to manage third-party model change risk.

positions.source_passage:
Local SLM Architecture: Where clinical utility permits, manufacturers should deploy domain-specific Small Language Models (SLMs) locally on-device or within private, locked environments.

Control of Update Cycles: Local hosting isolates the medical device from unannounced third-party API changes, ensuring that model weight updates occur exclusively through controlled, validated manufacturer release cycles.
positions.position_gist: Where clinical utility permits, manufacturers should deploy domain-specific small language models locally or in private locked environments so model updates occur only through controlled, validated manufacturer release cycles rather than unannounced third-party API changes.

positions.source_passage:
Version Support Matrix: Recognizing that healthcare facilities and clinical sites upgrade software asynchronously, local model locking shifts the operational burden to multi-version lifecycle management.

Quality System Expectations: The FDA should encourage manufacturers to incorporate strict backward-compatibility testing matrices, automated re-validation suites, and clear deprecation schedules directly into their Quality Management System (QMS) to support multiple active field baselines transparently during audits.
positions.position_gist: Because local model locking creates multi-version proliferation across asynchronously upgrading sites, FDA should encourage manufacturers to build backward-compatibility testing matrices, automated re-validation suites, and deprecation schedules into their QMS to manage multiple active field baselines.

positions.source_passage:
When reliance on hosted third-party foundation model APIs is unavoidable, manufacturers must establish proactive detection mechanisms to catch upstream model behavior shifts before they impact clinical care:

Golden Synthetic Benchmark Suites: Automated CI/CD pipelines running fixed, representative clinical benchmark datasets (prompts/inputs paired with expected standard outputs) on a regular cadence (e.g., daily/weekly) to flag output drift beyond clinical tolerance thresholds.

Semantic Drift Analysis: Embeddings-based tracking of production inputs and outputs to measure statistical similarity over time, catching subtle reasoning shifts or vocabulary changes.

Guardrail & Validator Telemetry: Real-time monitoring of post-processing guardrail trigger rates and rule-based validation failures to signal unexpected changes in model behavior.
positions.position_gist: Where hosted third-party model APIs must be used, manufacturers should run frequent automated 'golden' benchmark suites with clinical tolerance thresholds, embeddings-based semantic drift analysis, and real-time guardrail/validator telemetry to detect upstream behavior shifts before they affect care.

positions.source_passage:
The FDA should provide clear regulatory frameworks that:

Recognize localized version locking (e.g., on-edge SLMs) as an acceptable risk-mitigation strategy for change control under Premarket Approval (PMA) or 510(k) modifications.
positions.position_gist: FDA should explicitly recognize localized version locking (e.g., on-edge SLMs) as an acceptable change-control risk-mitigation strategy in PMA or 510(k) modification frameworks.

positions.source_passage: Define acceptable validation standards for continuous automated benchmarking when hosted third-party APIs are utilized.
positions.position_gist: FDA should define acceptable validation standards for continuous automated benchmarking when devices rely on hosted third-party model APIs.

positions.source_passage: Establish clear documentation expectations for supporting multi-version active deployments across fragmented clinical sites.
positions.position_gist: FDA should establish clear documentation expectations for supporting multiple simultaneously active device/model versions deployed across fragmented clinical sites.
